newsitem.title: CANADA: Chile's Frei in Canada to sign trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Frei in Canada to sign trade deal.

text.p: Chile's President Eduardo Frei arrived in Canada on Sunday ahead of Monday's signing of a free trade deal between the two countries.
Frei and his wife Marta Larraechea de Frei were greeted by Canada's Governor General Romeo LeBlanc, who is the country's titular head of state, and his wife Diana Fowler LeBlanc.

The bilateral trade pact calls for the removal of tariffs on 80 percent of trade between Chile and Canada as soon as it goes into effect, with most of the other tariffs being phased out over 15 years.
The deal also sets rules for trade in a wide range of services, including banking and telecommunications.

Frei and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien are to initial the agreement on Monday morning. The pact, which slashes trade barriers between the two countries, will not take effect until it has been translated into Spanish, English and French and has been approved by both countries' legislatures.
